review.explanation: The surface form 劉惔 is the full canonical name of Liu Tan (劉惔). The annotation text in sfh1-ev-23-rendan-033-liu-annotation-003 explicitly mentions 王濛劉惔共遊新亭 and 惔曰, confirming this person is Liu Tan. The candidate evidence from people.json provides the canonical name. No contradicting evidence exists.

The surface form 尚 is the abbreviated personal name of Xie Shang (謝尚). The annotation in sfh1-ev-23-rendan-033-liu-annotation-003 explicitly states 謝仁祖 and the alias evidence from aliases.json shows 謝仁祖 as the courtesy name of 謝尚. The main text mentions 謝鎮西徃尚書墓, and the annotation identifies 尚書 as 謝裒尚 (Xie Shang's father). The context of 尚 referring to Xie Shang is consistent with the annotation's identification of 謝仁祖 as 謝尚.

The surface form 尚 is the abbreviated personal name of Xie Shang (謝尚). The annotation in sfh1-ev-23-rendan-033-liu-annotation-004 states 尚初辭然已無歸意 and 惔曰仁祖韻中自應來, confirming that 尚 and 仁祖 refer to the same person, Xie Shang. The alias evidence from aliases.json confirms 謝仁祖 is the courtesy name of 謝尚. The reference semantics correctly identifies this as distinct from Liu Tan (劉惔).

The surface form 惔 is the abbreviated personal name of Liu Tan (劉惔). The annotation in sfh1-ev-23-rendan-033-liu-annotation-004 states 惔曰仁祖韻中自應來, where 惔 is the one speaking about 仁祖 (Xie Shang). The candidate evidence from people.json confirms 劉惔 as the canonical name. The reference semantics correctly identifies this as distinct from Xie Shang (謝尚).

The mention '之' is a pronoun referring to the person being invited (Xie Shang). The main text establishes 謝鎮西 (Xie Shang) as the subject who returns from the tomb visit, and the Liu annotation explicitly states 尚 (Xie Shang) is the one being invited (濛欲招尚). The pronoun resolution to Xie Shang is directly supported by the annotation evidence.

The surface form '濛' is the personal name of Wang Meng (王濛). The Liu annotation explicitly names 王濛 as one of the two people at Xinting (王濛劉惔共遊新亭), and the main text begins with 王劉 (Wang and Liu). The canonical name match from people.json directly supports this identification.

The surface form '王濛' is the full canonical name of Wang Meng. The Liu annotation explicitly places 王濛 at Xinting with 劉惔, matching the main text's opening 王劉共在杭南. The canonical name match from people.json directly supports this identification.

The surface form '謝仁祖' is the courtesy name of Xie Shang (謝尚). The Liu annotation explicitly states 謝仁祖 in the context of 濛欲招尚, and the annotation also uses 仁祖 as a direct reference to the same person (惔曰仁祖韻中自應來). The alias registry match to 謝尚 is directly corroborated by the annotation text.

The mention 仁祖 is the courtesy name of Xie Shang (謝尚). The candidate evidence from aliases.json explicitly states 仁祖 as a courtesy name for 謝尚. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-23-rendan-033-liu-annotation-003) explicitly glosses 謝仁祖 as 尚, confirming the identity. The main text context (sfh1-ev-23-rendan-033-main) describes 謝鎮西 (Xie Shang) going to his uncle's tomb, and the annotation confirms 謝裒 is the uncle (尚書謝裒尚), tying the narrative to Xie Shang. The annotation sfh1-ev-23-rendan-033-liu-annotation-004 explicitly uses 仁祖 to refer to the same person as 尚 in the narrative. No contradicting evidence exists. The identity is directly supported by the supplied evidence.
